content.value_statement: Agent tools often fail because descriptions, names, and responses are unclear. This skill helps teams design clearer tool APIs for Claude, Codex, and other assistants.
actual_capabilities: Explains how agents interpret tool names, descriptions, parameters, and responses.
Provides criteria for deciding when to consolidate or separate tools.
Shows how to structure tool descriptions with usage context and return details.
Guides response format design for concise and detailed outputs.
Defines error message patterns that help agents recover from failed calls.
Offers testing criteria for tool clarity, consistency, and recoverability.
limitations: It is guidance content and does not generate production tool code automatically.
It does not validate an existing MCP server or API implementation by itself.
It assumes the user can provide tool specs, failure examples, or workflow details.
It cannot replace security review for tools that execute commands or access sensitive data.

use_cases.title: Design a New Agent Tool
use_cases.description: Plan a tool contract with clear names, parameters, response formats, and recovery messages before implementation.

use_cases.title: Improve Confusing Tool Calls
use_cases.description: Review observed agent failures and rewrite tool descriptions to reduce ambiguity and incorrect calls.

use_cases.title: Standardize a Tool Collection
use_cases.description: Apply naming, grouping, and consolidation rules across related tools to make selection easier for agents.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Tool
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single tool specification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tool specification for agent usability. Check the name, description, parameters, return format, and error messages. Suggest concise improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a Tool Description
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate improvement of unclear tool documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this tool description so an agent knows when to use it, what inputs it accepts, what it returns, and how to recover from errors.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate a Tool Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this list of tools for overlap and ambiguity. Recommend which tools to merge, separate, rename, or keep unchanged, with reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Failure Modes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced optimization using real agent failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these agent requests, tool calls, and failures, identify the root design problems. Propose revised tool contracts and a focused test plan.

output_examples.input: A team has five search tools with similar names and agents often choose the wrong one.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend grouping related workflows, removing overlapping descriptions, and creating clearer selection rules for each tool.

output_examples.input: A customer lookup tool returns large records when the agent only needs confirmation.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest concise and detailed response modes, with description guidance for when each mode should be used.

output_examples.input: Agents fail when a tool returns a generic error after bad input.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend actionable errors that name the invalid field, explain the expected format, and guide a corrected retry.

best_practices: Write each tool description to answer what it does, when to use it, and what it returns.
Consolidate tools when separate options create unclear selection decisions for agents.
Test tool designs with realistic agent requests and revise based on observed failures.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague tool names or descriptions that force agents to guess intent.
Do not expose many overlapping tools when one workflow-level tool would be clearer.
Do not return generic errors that give agents no path to correction.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design tool APIs, descriptions, schemas, responses, and errors that agents can use reliably.

faq.question: Is this skill only for MCP tools?
faq.answer: No. It includes MCP naming guidance, but the design principles apply to most agent-facing tools.

faq.question: Can it write implementation code?
faq.answer: It focuses on design guidance. Users can apply the guidance before writing or revising implementation code.

faq.question: How does it improve tool reliability?
faq.answer: It reduces ambiguity in tool selection, parameter use, response interpretation, and error recovery.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Engineers, developer experience teams, and AI platform teams building tools for Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it perform live security checks?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation guidance and does not scan systems, run commands, or inspect live services.
